 $850 million of Growing Revenues

355% yy increase of net income to $403 million or $12.69 per share

Two-fold increase of 2027 semi-annual dividend

Potential Secondary Listing on the Singapore Exchange (SGX)

$3.6 billion in minimum contracted revenues

ATHENS, Greece, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TEN, Ltd (NYSE: TEN) (the “Company”) today reported results (unaudited) for the nine months and the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

NINE MONTHS 2026 SUMMARY RESULTS
During the first nine months of 2026, TEN, with an average in-the-water fleet of 63 vessels, generated gross revenues of $851 million, a near $274 million increase from the nine months of 2025.

The resulting net income for the first nine-months of 2026 reached $403 million equivalent to $12.69 per share compared to $2.75 per share in the nine-month period of 2025, representing a gross increase of 355%.

Operating income during the 2026 nine-month period and inclusive of a $94 million capital gain from the sale of four vessels, rose to $467 million from $171 million in the corresponding period of 2025, which also included capital gains of $12.5 million.

Adjusted EBITDA for the first nine months of 2026 was at $510 million from $289 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Despite having 12 vessels on scheduled dry dock, one vessel undergoing repairs and some on repositing voyages during the first nine months of 2026, fleet utilization remained high at 95.5%.

The average Time Charter Equivalent (TCE) rate per vessel per day for the nine months of 2026 rose to $45,170, compared with $30,703 in the nine months of 2025, representing a 47% increase, reflecting the continued strength of the tanker markets.

Total operating expenses per vessel per day remained at a still competitive $10,664 in the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Depreciation and amortization in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, totaled $135 million from $126 million in the corresponding 2025 period, attributable to the operation of a slightly larger fleet consisting of newer and larger class vessels.

TEN’s cash balances at the end of September 2026, stood at a healthy $533.5 million, $269 million higher than the cash levels at the end of September 2025

Total bank debt as of September 30, 2026, was $2.0 billion from $1.8 billion at September 30, 2025, reflecting new loans associated with vessels entering the fleet.

Interest and finance costs for the first nine months of 2026 amounted to $65.7 million, about $7.0 million lower than the level recorded in the first nine-months of 2025, as a result of decreased spreads attained from banks for new or refinanced loans and lower global interest rates. Interest income rose to f $10.4 million in the 2026 nine-month period compared to $7.7 million received in the 2025 nine-month period.

Q3 2026 SUMMARY RESULTS
With an average fleet of 63 vessels, TEN’s gross revenues during the third quarter of 2026 approximated $300 million, an increase of $113 million, or 61%, over the corresponding 2025 period.

Net income in the third quarter of 2026 reached $174.5 million (inclusive of the capital gains mentioned above), equivalent to $5.57 per share, from $1.05 per share in the third quarter of 2025 which also recorded the aforementioned capital gains. A 431% increase.

Operating income during the third quarter of 2026, inclusive of $56.2 million capital gain from the sale of three vessels in the summer of 2026, settled at $194.5 million from $60.5 million in the equivalent quarter of 2025, which included capital gains of $8.9 million obtained from the sale of three vessels

Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was at $185.4 million, 94% higher from the 2025 third quarter level.

Average TCE rate per vessel per day in the third quarter of 2026 reached $48,615, 59% higher than the 2025 equivalent period, supported by high fleet utilization rates of nearly 94%.

Operating expenses per vessel per day in the third quarter of 2026 were $11,394.

Depreciation and amortization expenses during the third quarter of 2026 were in line with the increased number of vessels in the fleet at $44.8 million, just $2.3 million higher than the 2025 third quarter levels.

Consistent with the first nine-months trend, interest and finance costs in the third quarter of 2026 decreased by $1.4 million from the corresponding 2025 period to $22.3 million, benefiting from lower borrowing spreads and lower global interest rates, while interest income totaled $4.8 million.

SUBSEQUENT EVENTS & OTHERS
On September 29, 2026, TEN exercised its right to repurchase the 2022-built LNG carrier Tenergy, currently under a five-year finance lease, at a significant discount to fair market value. The acquisition will be completed upon the expiration of the lease in January 2027 and will be financed in its entirety through funds obtained from an international banking institution on attractive terms.

On October 26, 2026, TEN announced its authorization to commence an up to $150 million buyback program covering both common and preferred shares. The timing of any share purchases of any type, the prices and the exact number of shares to be purchased will depend on prevailing market conditions, cash balances and other uses of capital.

TEN is evaluating the possibility of applying to list its common shares on the Main Board of the Singapore Exchange Securities Trading Limited (the “SGX-ST”). TEN’s common shares are currently listed and traded on the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) and would continue to be primarily listed and traded on NYSE.  No final decision or commitment has been made as to the timing, terms or conditions of any such listing on the SGX-ST.

CORPORATE AFFAIRS

On October 26, 2026, TEN announced a doubling of its first 2027 semi-annual common stock dividend to $1.00 per share, up from $0.50 per share in the 2026 comparable period. The dividend is scheduled for payment on January 20, 2027, to shareholders of record as of January 12, 2027. For the entire 2026, TEN paid common shareholders a total of $1.50 per share in dividends.

Since the Company’s NYSE listing in 2002, TEN has consistently demonstrated its commitment to reward shareholders, and will have distributed, until the end of 2026 over $1.0 billion in aggregate common and preferred share dividends.

The Company’s 9.25% Series E Preferred Shares become redeemable at the election of the Company on May 28, 2027, and the Company currently expects that it may elect to redeem, all or a portion of, such Series E Preferred Shares on the above stated date. This disclosure does not constitute a notice of redemption, and there can be no assurance as to the amount, if any, of the Series E Preferred Shares that will be redeemed.

CORPORATE STRATEGY

As tanker market fundamentals, in terms of supply and demand remain healthy and continue to be supported by trade dislocations stemming from geopolitics, TEN benefits from the very strong conditions evident both in the freight market and the firm asset values.

Accordingly, TEN continues to capture the market upside through spot and profit-sharing contracts, while pursuing long-term charter coverage at today’s high levels.

With cash balances well in excess of half a billion dollars, and $3.6 billion of future revenues, management remains committed to evaluating accretive growth opportunities across the various sectors in which TEN operates, while continuing to focus on the divestment of older assets where demand remains strong.

“TEN is navigating through this unprecedented environment with a diversified and high-quality fleet, positioned to capture market upside by securing firm forward revenues and providing shareholders with attractive returns. In parallel, it is continuing its dynamic 20-vessel newbuilding program,” stated Mr. George Saroglou, COO and President of TEN. “The doubling of the 2027 first semi-annual dividend, the $150 million buyback program together with the divestment of older tonnage highlights management’s intention to use TEN’s healthy and growing cash balances for the long-term benefit of the Company, and its shareholders,” To this end, and having been pioneers in the capital markets with a first public listing back in 1993 on the Oslo Bors, and in 2002 on the NYSE, management currently evaluates a possible secondary listing on the Singapore Exchange (SGX), in order to position the Company in the growing Asian capital market going forward” Mr. Saroglou concluded.

Alongside its leadership position in Canada, Decibel is a significant and growing participant in international cannabis markets. Decibel operates a processing and manufacturing facility in Calgary, Alberta, a cultivation facility in Battleford, Saskatchewan, and an EU-GMP licensed cultivation and processing facility in Chatham, Ontario.

New Patent Strengthens Cingulate’s Intellectual Property Portfolio While Company Maintains Focus on Advancing Lead ADHD Candidate CTx-1301

KANSAS CITY, Kan., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cingulate Inc. (NASDAQ: CING), a biopharmaceutical company utilizing its proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) drug delivery platform to develop a pipeline of next-generation pharmaceutical products, today announced that the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has issued U.S. Patent No. 12,797,335, titled "Trimodal, Precision-Timed Release Tablet."

The newly issued patent covers a buspirone tablet formulation incorporating Cingulate's proprietary PTR™ technology, which is designed to release medication at three separate, predetermined times throughout the day from a single tablet. Buspirone is an FDA-approved treatment for anxiety disorders. The patented formulation supports the Company's development of CTx-2103 and further demonstrates the versatility and broader applicability of Cingulate's technology beyond its initial focus on ADHD.

"Cingulate remains focused on advancing CTx-1301, our lead ADHD treatment candidate, toward NDA resubmission and commercialization in the second half of 2027, if approved. We believe CTx-2103 represents an attractive opportunity to build a pipeline of assets beyond ADHD with our proprietary PTR™ Platform. The issuance of this patent further strengthens the Company’s intellectual property portfolio. Following approval of CTx-1301, Cingulate anticipates initiating the development of CTx-2103," said Cingulate Chairman and CEO Shane J. Schaffer.

About U.S. Patent No. 12,797,335

U.S. Patent No. 12,797,335, titled "Trimodal, Precision-Timed Release Tablet," was issued by the United States Patent and Trademark Office on November 17, 2026. The patent covers a pharmaceutical tablet formulation designed to deliver three separate releases of an active pharmaceutical ingredient at predetermined intervals following administration. The patented technology utilizes Cingulate's proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) approach to control the timing of medication release from a single oral dosage form. The patent covers a buspirone formulation relevant to Cingulate's investigational CTx-2103 candidate for the treatment of anxiety disorders and further expands the Company's intellectual property portfolio surrounding its proprietary drug delivery technology.

About Anxiety

Anxiety disorders are the most common category of mental disorders in the United States, affecting nearly 30 percent of adults at some point during their lives, according to the American Psychiatric Association.¹ Anxiety is a normal response to stress or perceived danger and can help individuals prepare for challenging situations. However, when excessive anxiety becomes persistent, difficult to control, and interferes with everyday activities, it may constitute an anxiety disorder.² According to the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), an estimated 31.1 percent of U.S. adults experience an anxiety disorder at some point during their lives.³ Despite the availability of effective treatments, anxiety disorders frequently go undiagnosed or untreated, with research indicating that delays between the onset of symptoms and initial treatment can extend for many years.⁴ The COVID-19 pandemic further highlighted the growing burden of mental health conditions, with the World Health Organization reporting a 25 percent increase in the global prevalence of anxiety and depression during the first year of the pandemic.⁵

About CTx-2103

CTx-2103 utilizes a novel multi-core formulation of buspirone, an FDA-approved treatment for anxiety.

CTx-2103 will be designed as a once-daily, modified-release tablet with clear differentiation and compelling advantages over standard treatment options which must be taken multiple times per day to maximize efficacy.

Cingulate completed a proof-of-concept study in which pharmacokinetics were evaluated for a trimodal tablet providing three precisely timed doses of buspirone. In addition, scintigraphic imaging visualized transit of the tablet through the gastrointestinal tract to confirm both the site and onset of release, which was then correlated with pharmacokinetic data to establish the full release profile of the CTx-2103 formulation. Based on the pharmacokinetic profile seen in the data, CTx-2103 achieved a triple release of buspirone. These results provided the critical information required to complete a Pre-IND meeting with FDA to discuss the design of the clinical and regulatory program.

About Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)

ADHD is a chronic neurobiological and developmental disorder that affects millions of children and often continues into adulthood. The estimated market size of the US ADHD market is approximately 100 million annual prescriptions. The condition is marked by an ongoing pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development. In the U.S., over 20 million patients have been diagnosed with ADHD. Among this group, 12 million are adults and over 8 million are under the age of 17. According to the CDC, just 53.6 percent of all children and teens with ADHD reported they were actively treating their symptoms with medication in 2022, with 65-90 percent demonstrating clinical ADHD symptoms that persist into adulthood. Current market trends demonstrate that adult ADHD prevalence is larger and growing faster than the child and adolescent segments combined.

About CTx-1301

CTx-1301 (dexmethylphenidate HCl) is a once-daily, multi-core tablet utilizing Cingulate’s proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) platform to deliver three precisely timed releases of active medication across the day. This design aims to provide rapid onset of effect and entire active-day duration. CTx-1301 is being evaluated for the treatment of ADHD under the FDA’s 505(b)(2) pathway. In October 2025, the FDA accepted for review the NDA for CTx-1301 and assigned a PDUFA target action date of May 31, 2026. On June 1, 2026, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter for the CTx-1301 NDA; the Company and its CDMO have since substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the CMC requests, and the Company expects to resubmit the NDA between December 2026 and January 2026. There can be no assurance regarding the timing of any resubmission or whether approval will occur.

About Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) Platform Technology

Cingulate is developing ADHD and anxiety disorder product candidates capable of achieving true once-daily dosing using Cingulate’s innovative PTR drug delivery platform technology. It incorporates a proprietary Erosion Barrier Layer (EBL) providing control of drug release at precise, pre-defined times with no release of drug prior to the intended release. The EBL technology is enrobed around a drug-containing core to give a tablet-in-tablet dose form. It is designed to erode at a controlled rate until eventually the drug is released from the core tablet. The EBL formulation, Oralogik™, is licensed from BDD Pharma. Cingulate intends to utilize its PTR technology to expand and augment its clinical-stage pipeline by identifying and developing additional product candidates in other therapeutic areas in addition to Anxiety and ADHD.

About Cingulate Inc.

Cingulate Inc. (NASDAQ: CING) is a biopharmaceutical company utilizing its proprietary PTR drug delivery platform technology to build and advance a pipeline of next-generation pharmaceutical products, designed to improve the lives of patients suffering from frequently diagnosed conditions characterized by burdensome daily dosing regimens and suboptimal treatment outcomes. With an initial focus on the treatment of ADHD, Cingulate is identifying and evaluating additional therapeutic areas where PTR technology may be employed to develop future product candidates, including to treat anxiety disorders. Cingulate is headquartered in Kansas City. For more information, visit Cingulate.com.

Miami, FL, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ONAR Holding Corporation (OTCID: ONAR) (“ONAR” or the “Company”), an AI-powered marketing platform, today filed its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and issued the following letter to stockholders from Chief Executive Officer Claude Zdanow.

Dear Fellow Stockholders,

In July, I gave you four priorities and said we would report on each one as it moved from plan to fact. Four months later, three of them are fact: the acquisition, the financing that paid for it, and the exchange of certain of our lenders’ older debt into the same convertible notes issued in the financing. The fourth, a listing of our common stock on a national securities exchange (a “listing”), is where the work is now.

The short version:

  • What we bought. Advertise Purple LLC (“Advertise Purple”), a leader in affiliate and partnership marketing and a business more than three times our size by revenue.
  • How to read the report we filed today. We owned Advertise Purple for two days of the quarter. On a pro forma basis for the full nine months, revenue would have been $13.5 million, not the $3.1 million we reported.
  • The cash. A nine-month net loss of $3.61 million, but only $0.59 million of cash used in operations.
  • What the company was valued at. $25 million pre-money and before any debt converts, which implies about $36 million to $40 million for the combined company once the debt converts. One fixed price, $0.038576 per share. Holders of our existing preferred stock intend to exchange into the same class.
  • The debt. Total liabilities of $37.7 million. About $15 million can potentially become equity on a listing: $11.0 million would convert to preferred stock automatically, and $3.9 million of senior convertible notes can convert at the holders’ election. Approximately $16.4 million is the purchase price for Advertise Purple that we agreed to pay over time. The cash paid at closing was funded largely with the September notes, short-term funding that we intend to convert to equity or refinance.
  • The companies are already working together. JUICE and Advertise Purple are cross-selling and driving new business for each other.
  • What comes next. A Nasdaq listing, which is not assured, and the 1-for-250 reverse stock split approved for it.

What we bought

On September 29 we acquired Advertise Purple, a business more than three times our size by revenue. Advertise Purple is a leader in affiliate and partnership marketing, one of the fastest-growing channels in digital marketing and one in which clients pay primarily for measured outcomes. It manages performance-based programs for a roster of established, well-recognized brands. It fits what ONAR is: an AI-powered marketing platform that acquires specialist marketing companies and runs them on shared technology, so that growth-stage and middle-market brands sell more of their products and services online. Together, our operating companies now serve approximately 400 clients. Cortex, our attribution platform, began billing subscription clients in July and has completed its first full quarter of recurring billings. That revenue is not yet material, but it is the first recurring technology revenue ONAR Labs has generated. With Advertise Purple we also acquired Bloom, its affiliate performance data platform.

How to read the report we filed today

Our third quarter report includes two days of Advertise Purple results and all of the debt from buying it. Note 2 of the Form 10-Q shows what revenue and net income would have been if we had owned Advertise Purple since January 1, 2025.

 Three months ended September 30, 2026Nine months ended September 30, 2026
Revenue, as reported$1.06 million$3.13 million
Pro Forma Revenue, as if we had owned Advertise Purple since January 1, 2025$4.44 million$13.52 million
Net loss, as reported$(1.36) million$(3.61) million
Pro Forma Net loss, as if we had owned Advertise Purple since January 1, 2025$(0.61) million$(1.25) million

Source: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, condensed consolidated statements of operations and Note 2. The figures above, including Pro Forma amounts, are unaudited.

With Advertise Purple for the full period, pro forma nine-month revenue would have been $13.5 million, more than four times the $3.1 million we reported. Those figures combine two companies for a period before we owned one of them, and they are not a forecast. They do not include the interest on the acquisition debt, and they do not include any cost savings or synergies from combining the two companies. ONAR without the acquisition of Advertise Purple was already improving results: reported revenue grew 68% for the nine months, general and administrative expense fell 55%, and the loss from operations narrowed by 60%.

The cash

The cash picture is much better than the reported loss. For the nine months we reported a net loss of $3.61 million, but the business used only $0.59 million of cash in operations. Nearly three quarters of the loss was interest expense, and most of that interest was not paid in cash.

What the company was valued at

The investors in our September 28, 2026 financings, which funded the Advertise Purple acquisition, priced ONAR at $25 million pre-money and before any debt converts. Upon a listing, their convertible notes and the convertible notes our lenders exchanged older debt into become one class of preferred stock, Series 1. The Series 1 Preferred Stock converts into common stock at one fixed price, $0.038576 per share, which does not move with the market. On those terms, the equity after a listing would be valued at about $36 million once those notes convert, and about $40 million if the senior notes, which can convert on the same terms, convert as well. The $25 million is the value before any of that debt becomes equity. The to is the implied value of the combined company, including Advertise Purple, after the conversion of debt. The holders of our existing Series B, C and E preferred stock, including holders who also invested in the September 28 financings, intend to exchange into Series 1 Preferred Stock at the time of the listing, and the financing documents anticipate that exchange. However, definitive agreements regarding the preferred exchange are not yet signed and so it is not assured.

The $25 million valuation and the conversion terms are what the investors in the September 28 financings agreed to in their purchase agreements. That valuation is not the market value of our stock or a prediction of it, and conversion means more shares outstanding. The Form 10-Q has the detail, including the warrants issued with the financing.

The debt

Total liabilities are $37.7 million, up from $9.7 million at the start of the year. The table shows the three largest pieces, with the notes at face value. The rest includes accounts payable and accrued expenses of about , deferred revenue, warrant liabilities, and older notes and settlements on fixed payment schedules.

What it isAmountWhat happens to it
Senior convertible notes$3.9 millionDue September 2027. We are actively engaged with multiple lenders, through a placement agent, on a senior credit facility to refinance them, though a refinancing is not assured. Senior noteholders are also able to elect to convert into Series 1 preferred stock upon a listing.
Convertible notes that become equity on a listing$11.0 millionDue March 2028. Convert automatically into Series 1 preferred stock upon a listing. No cash repayment, after the conversion into preferred stock. $7.1 million of this is older debt our lenders exchanged, not new borrowing.
Purchase price for Advertise Purple, paid over time$16.4 millionA $7.0 million note to the sellers, $5.0 million in deferred payments from the closing, of which $2.4 million has been paid since quarter-end, and an earnout recorded at a provisional fair value of $4.4 million, up to a maximum of $8.0 million if all earnout milestones are met. It is owed only if the business reaches its gross profit targets per the acquisition agreement.

Notes are shown at face value. The balance sheet carries the senior convertible notes at $3.2 million and the $11.0 million of convertible notes at $8.5 million, net of unamortized discounts, and the difference is recognized as non-cash interest expense over the life of the notes. The earnout is at the provisional fair value recorded in the Form 10-Q.

The $11.0 million of junior secured convertible notes were structured so that they can become preferred stock at the time of a listing, instead of being repaid in cash, and holders of the senior convertible notes may elect to convert to preferred stock on the same terms at the listing, so up to about $15 million of this can potentially become equity. The purchase price in the table is the part of the price for Advertise Purple that we agreed to pay over time. The cash we paid at closing, about $7.6 million, was funded largely with the proceeds of the senior and junior notes above. That is short-term funding: the junior notes convert to equity on a listing, and the senior notes can convert or be refinanced. The earnout is owed only if Advertise Purple reaches certain contractual milestones, and we intend to pay the seller note and the deferred payments from the cash the combined business generates.

None of that makes the debt go away. We ended the quarter with a working capital deficit of about $15.2 million, our filings continue to say there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern, and a listing is not assured. If our listing does not happen, the $11.0 million of convertible notes will remain outstanding and mature in March 2028.

The companies are already working together

JUICE now runs Advertise Purple’s marketing and is bringing it new business, and Advertise Purple’s sales team sends leads to JUICE every month. We are bringing our technology, ONAR AI and Cortex, to Advertise Purple’s teams and clients. Advertise Purple continues to be led by its core team, five of whom signed employment agreements with us at the acquisition.

What comes next

We are pursuing a listing of our common stock on the Nasdaq Capital Market and are in the application and preparation stage. Approval is not assured. A listing requires a higher share price than ours, so a 1-for-250 reverse stock split was approved in October by our board of directors and by the required stockholder vote. The split is not yet effective. It changes the number of shares you hold, not your percentage of the company, and the $0.038576 conversion price of the Series 1 preferred stock adjusts by the same ratio.

The milestones to watch from here are the reverse split taking effect, Nasdaq’s decision on our application, and a senior credit facility to refinance the senior notes, none of which is assured, and then our annual report, the first that will include a full quarter of Advertise Purple.

A year ago, our third quarter revenue was $0.66 million. Counting Advertise Purple for the full quarter, on a pro forma basis this year’s third quarter revenue would have been $4.4 million. The first full quarter together with Advertise Purple is under way.

Thank you for staying with us.

Sincerely,

Claude Zdanow
Chief Executive Officer
ONAR Holding Corporation

ONAR (OTCID: ONAR), pronounced “honor,” is an AI-powered marketing platform. ONAR acquires specialist marketing companies serving middle-market and growth-stage brands across performance marketing, creative, and commerce, and operates them as one company on shared proprietary technology designed to automate up to 70% of manual marketing work. Its technology division, ONAR Labs, develops and houses the Company’s proprietary technology, including ONAR AI, a marketing intelligence platform deployed across the Company’s operating companies to improve productivity; Retina AI, a predictive customer intelligence platform; and Cortex, an offline and online sales attribution platform. SAN DIEGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Halozyme Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: HALO) (Halozyme), today provided an update on the German preliminary injunction hearing that overturned the decision issued in December 2025, ordering Merck to refrain from distributing and offering Keytruda SC in Germany.

"We are disappointed that the Higher Regional Court overturned the preliminary injunction halting the launch of Keytruda SC in Germany. We disagree with the decision and will immediately file an infringement lawsuit against Merck in Germany seeking permanent relief, which is not precluded by today's decision," said Mark Snyder, Chief Legal Officer of Halozyme.

Separately and independently, in October 2026, a Dutch patent court prohibited Merck's European Marketing Approval holder from committing an infringement in Belgium, Denmark, France, Ireland, Italy, Sweden, Switzerland and the Netherlands, by manufacturing or causing to be manufactured, offering, putting on the market or using Keytruda SC in those countries, or by importing it or holding it in stock for that purpose.

The patents at issue arise from Halozyme's extensive research into nearly 7,000 modifications to human hyaluronidases. Among their uses, these hyaluronidases pioneered by Halozyme provide a mechanism for the rapid SC administration of therapeutic drugs. Halozyme's comprehensive studies and innovations were a significant advancement to the field of human-derived hyaluronidases.

The MDASE™ patents are not included in Halozyme's ENHANZE® licensing program and are distinct from its ENHANZE® patents. Halozyme is a biopharmaceutical company advancing disruptive solutions to improve patient experiences and outcomes for emerging and established therapies. TOOELE, Utah--(BUSINESS WIRE)--GenFlat Holdings, Inc. (OTCQB: GFLT), a developer of innovative collapsible shipping containers, today announced a 90-day commercial trial beginning in December 2026 with Ramps Logistics Limited, a Trinidad-based provider of integrated logistics and supply chain solutions serving customers throughout the Caribbean and international markets. The trial will evaluate the operational and economic benefits of GenFlat’s patented 40-foot collapsible shipping containers in Caribbean logistics operations with the potential to convert to container sales or leases in the future.

The trial agreement with Ramps Logistics follows GenFlat’s formation of a strategic collaboration with the Port Management Association of the Caribbean (PMAC), as we previously announced on July 23, 2026 on behalf of its 29 member ports endorsing GenFlat's collapsible containers earlier this year. GenFlat and PMAC will jointly host a live demonstration at the Port of St. John's in Antigua on December 10, 2026, showcasing the technology to regional port authorities, shipping lines, and logistics providers.

The Caribbean presents a compelling opportunity for GenFlat’s technology, as regional shipping networks face challenges associated with repositioning empty containers, limited port space, and high transportation costs. GenFlat containers are designed to collapse when empty, allowing four empty containers to be transported and stored in the space traditionally required for a single conventional container.

Through the trial, Ramps Logistics will assess how GenFlat’s containers can be integrated into its regional logistics operations, with a focus on reducing empty container repositioning costs, optimizing storage capacity, and improving overall supply chain efficiency. The trial will also provide GenFlat with valuable operational data and an opportunity to demonstrate its technology in a strategically important market.

“The Caribbean represents a significant market opportunity for GenFlat because of the unique logistical challenges associated with moving cargo between islands and repositioning empty containers,” said Drew Hall, Chief Executive Officer of GenFlat. “This trial represents an important step toward demonstrating how our technology can deliver measurable cost savings and operational efficiencies while establishing a foundation for broader adoption throughout the Caribbean.”

“We are constantly exploring innovative solutions that can improve logistics efficiency and deliver meaningful value to our customers,” said Rudy Rampersad, Vice President of Regional Initiatives at Ramps Logistics. “GenFlat’s collapsible container technology has the potential to address some of the longstanding challenges associated with container transportation and storage in the Caribbean. We look forward to evaluating its performance in real-world operations and exploring opportunities for a broader commercial relationship.”

Following completion of the trial, GenFlat and Ramps Logistics intend to evaluate opportunities for an expanded commercial relationship, including potential deployment of GenFlat containers across additional Caribbean shipping routes.

GenFlat Holdings, Inc. (OTCQB: GFLT) is an innovative logistics technology company focused on transforming global container shipping through its patented collapsible shipping containers. DALLAS, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Argent Trust Company, as the trustee (the "Trustee") of the San Juan Basin Royalty Trust (the "Trust") (NYSE: SJT), today reported that it will not declare a monthly cash distribution to the holders of its units of beneficial interest (the "Unit Holders") due to excess production costs incurred during prior periods for the Trust's royalty interest burdening the subject interests ("Subject Interests"), as well as continued low natural gas pricing. Excess production costs occur when production costs and capital expenditures exceed the gross proceeds for a certain period. The balance of cumulative excess production costs is currently approximately $12,933,840 gross ($9,700,380 net to the Trust), an increase in the deficit of $510,821 gross ($383,116 net to the Trust) from last month's reporting period.  Hilcorp will continue to charge the balance of excess production costs to the Trust's net proceeds each month. Until the balance is paid in full, the Trust will not receive royalty income as all net proceeds will be applied to the balance of excess production costs.  No cash distributions will be made by the Trust until future net proceeds are sufficient to (a) repay the balance of excess production costs, accrued as a result of Hilcorp San Juan L.P.'s drilling of two new horizontal wells in 2024, (b) replenish a reserve in the amount of $2,000,000, and (c) repay the principal and interest on the Trust's line of credit at Texas Bank ("Line of Credit"), after which time, the Trust will resume distributions of the royalty income to the holders of the Trust's units of beneficial interest. 

Hilcorp reported $4,588,173 of total revenue from the Subject Interests for the production month of September 2026, consisting of $4,515,139 of gas revenues, and $73,034 of oil revenues.

For the Subject Interests, Hilcorp reported $5,098,994 of production costs (excluding the balance of excess production costs) for the production month of September 2026, consisting of $3,149,531 of lease operating expenses, $455,943 of severance taxes, and $1,493,520 of capital costs.  

Based upon information provided to the Trust by Hilcorp, gas volumes for the Subject Interests for September 2026 totaled 1,970,343 Mcf (2,189,269 MMBtu), as compared to 2,057,618 Mcf (2,286,242 MMBtu), for August 2026. Dividing gas revenues by production volume yielded an average gas price for September 2026 of $2.29 per Mcf ($2.06 per MMBtu), an increase of $0.01 per Mcf ($0.01 per MMBtu) as compared to the average gas price for August 2026 of $2.28 per Mcf ($2.05 per MMBtu).

This month's Trust administrative expenses totaled $56,216. The decrease in administrative expenses was attributable to differences in timing of the receipt and payment of certain expenses by the Trust.  Interest income in the amount of $12 and a draw of $56,204 from the Line of Credit will be used to pay the balance of Trust administrative expenses for the month of November which will bring the outstanding principal balance on the Line of Credit to $1,211,705.

Pursuant to the Amended and Restated Royalty Trust Indenture, dated December 12, 2007 (as amended on February 15, 2024, by the First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Royalty Trust Indenture), the Trustee is authorized to retain, in its sole discretion, a cash reserve for payment of Trust liabilities that are contingent or uncertain or otherwise not currently due and payable. Cash reserves were utilized to pay interest accrued on the Line of Credit each month from July 2025 through May 2026.  The balance of cash reserves maintained by the Trust is unchanged from the prior month. To align with the Trust's reporting on Form 10-Q, beginning with this news release, the reported balance of cash reserves includes cash held in the Trust's operating account and is $4,019.

Production from the Subject Interests continues to be gathered, processed, and sold under market sensitive and customary agreements.  The Trustee continues to engage with Hilcorp regarding its ongoing accounting and reporting to the Trust, and the Trust's third-party compliance auditors continue to audit payments made by Hilcorp to the Trust, inclusive of sales revenues, production costs, capital expenditures, adjustments, actualizations, and recoupments.  The Trust's auditing process has also included detailed analysis of Hilcorp's pricing and rates charged.  As previously disclosed in the Trust's filings, these revenues and costs (along with all costs) are the subject of the Trust's ongoing comprehensive audit process by the Trust's professional consultants and outside counsel to analyze compliance with all the underlying operative Trust agreements and evaluate potential remedies in the event there is suspected non-compliance.

As of October 20, 2026, the Trust resumed distributing monthly press releases via wire.  The Trust will continue to furnish unitholders with information through its website and Form 8-K filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, which are available at www.sec.gov.  If anyone would like to receive the press release via email, please contact the Trustee to be placed on the monthly press release email list.

MESA, Ariz., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Verra Mobility Corporation (NASDAQ: VRRM), a leading provider of smart mobility technology solutions, announced today that the City of San Jose has approved a contract with the company to design, build, operate, and maintain a speed safety program across the city. Under the agreement, Verra Mobility will deploy speed safety cameras across 33 systems at high-injury and high-speed corridors throughout San Jose.

San Jose joins Glendale, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland, and San Francisco as the six California cities authorized to pilot speed safety camera systems under Assembly Bill 645. Already, programs are experiencing success with a 79% reduction in speeding reported in San Francisco; Oakland reports an initial 70% reduction in speeding, stating this leads to 20,000 fewer speeding vehicles every day on city streets.

"Speeding is a major cause of fatal and severe-injury crashes in San José, and addressing dangerous speeds is essential to make our city safer," said John Ristow, director of transportation, City of San José. "Speed safety cameras will help us reduce speeding on some of our highest-risk streets and protect the people who live, work, and travel through our city."

The program is intended to slow down drivers and create safer streets for the community. To ensure the public is informed, a public education campaign has begun to educate drivers and community members about the program and its goals. Starting as early as December 14, drivers traveling 11 miles per hour or more over the posted speed limit will receive a warning notice. The warning period will continue until 60 days after the last camera is activated, then notice of violations will be issued starting at $50.

"Verra Mobility is proud to support the City of San Jose as it addresses speeding on some of the city's most high-risk corridors," said TJ Tiedje, vice president of sales, Verra Mobility. "This program is designed to give drivers clear notice and an opportunity to change their behavior, while helping the city create safer streets for everyone who uses them."

Unlike broader vehicle-monitoring and surveillance technologies, the program is narrowly focused on reducing dangerous speeding at designated locations and operates within AB 645's requirements for data protections, equitable fines, and a mandatory warning period. Citations are civil, carry no license points, and cannot be used for unrelated law enforcement or immigration purposes.

Verra Mobility has helped bring innovative traffic safety solutions to California communities for decades. As the sixth and final city authorized under AB 645, San Jose rounds out California's speed safety pilot program, and Verra Mobility now supports all six participating cities, giving each the benefit of the company's experience across the state. The company also helped launch and operate California's first red-light safety program under SB 720 in Mountain House, making it uniquely qualified to implement legislatively complex programs that require security and privacy safeguards.

Tegucigalpa will be a brand-new destination for JetBlue and its second in Honduras, further strengthening the airline’s growing network across Latin America and the Caribbean.

Flights to Grand Cayman will begin February 23, 2027, followed by Tegucigalpa on February 25. JetBlue will also offer limited-time daily nonstop service between Fort Lauderdale and Port of Spain from January 29 through February 15, giving customers a convenient option to travel to Trinidad and Tobago for the country's popular Carnival celebrations.¹

“We're grateful for the way customers across South Florida continue to embrace JetBlue, and we're committed to delivering even more of the destinations and travel options they're looking for,” said Daniel Shurz, senior vice president, revenue, network and enterprise planning, JetBlue. “With new international service to Honduras and Grand Cayman, we're strengthening Fort Lauderdale's role as a key gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean, making it easier for customers to reconnect with loved ones, explore new places and travel across our growing network.”

The new routes will also provide convenient connections through Fort Lauderdale to additional destinations across JetBlue's network.

New service to Tegucigalpa expands JetBlue's presence in Honduras, complementing existing flights between Fort Lauderdale and San Pedro Sula. Meanwhile, Grand Cayman adds another nonstop option to one of the Caribbean's most popular leisure destinations.

JetBlue expects to operate more than 150 daily departures from Fort Lauderdale during peak periods this winter, its largest schedule ever at FLL. PNC checking clients can borrow between $5,000 and $35,000 through a streamlined digital experience with typical access to their funds within minutes of finalizing their loan. Whether clients are managing an unexpected expense or pursuing an important goal, we're helping them access the funds they need with greater confidence, convenience and control."

With the ability to check rates without impacting their credit score, plus a fixed interest rate and predictable monthly payment, clients know exactly what to expect throughout the life of the loan, making it easier to budget and plan.

The new experience makes PNC Personal Loans available to more PNC checking clients nationwide. It is now offered in 49 states, including Washington, D.C., and is planning the launch in Florida in December.

"At PNC, we recognize every borrowing need is different," Allan said. "That's why we've designed the PNC Personal Loan to be straightforward from application through repayment, with clear terms, predictable payments and the support clients expect from PNC. BOSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Skillsoft® (NYSE: SKIL), a leading AI-native Skills Management Platform, today announced it has been named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Employee Experience – Learning Experience Management (LXM) 2026 Vendor Assessment.1

This recognition builds on Skillsoft’s position as a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: North America IT Training Services 2025-2026 Vendor Assessment2 and IDC MarketScape: European IT Training Services 2025 Vendor Assessment3. Skillsoft believes these recognitions reflect its strength across learning experience and IT training, two critical components of how organizations build workforce capability.

As AI, technology and business priorities change, so do the capabilities organizations need to execute. Leaders need a clear view of the capabilities they have today and what they will need next. Skills Management expands the role of learning by connecting workforce development more directly to business needs. The Skillsoft Percipio Platform enables organizations to identify critical skills, build and validate those capabilities, and put them to work against business priorities.

“Learning experience management is evolving as organizations zoom in on skills deficits and leverage skills apart from roles to continuously optimize how employees contribute to outcomes,” said Zachary Chertok, Research Director for HCM Applications and Agents at IDC.

What the recognition means for Skills Management

Skillsoft believes this IDC MarketScape assessment reflects the need to build capabilities that hold up, such as:

  • Proficiency, not completions: Skills mapping grounded in AI-powered assessments of what employees can demonstrate, rather than self-reported or completion data.
  • Development that builds on existing skills: Courses organized around employees’ current competencies and required skills, so people skip redundant training.
  • Learning built around real roles: Structured, multimodal journeys that go beyond content playlists to how people develop complex work.
  • Practice for the real thing: CAISY, Skillsoft’s conversational AI simulator, lets learners rehearse difficult conversations in a safe environment.

Together, these strengths show how learning is evolving beyond course completion to measure what employees can actually do.

“Every business priority depends on capability, and too often leaders lack a clear view of whether they have what they need to execute,” said Raianne Reiss, Chief Marketing and Sustainability Officer at Skillsoft. “Learning is foundational to building that capability, and its value grows when organizations can prove the skills that drive impact. We believe this recognition from IDC MarketScape reinforces the strength of the learning experience at the heart of Skillsoft’s broader Skills Management Platform.”

Learn more and access the IDC MarketScape excerpt, here.

About Skillsoft®

Skillsoft (NYSE: SKIL) is a global leader in Skills Management for the human + AI era. The AI-native Skillsoft Platform gives a clear view of workforce capability, closes critical skill gaps and proves the impact of skills on business outcomes. With Skillsoft, organizations can build AI-ready teams, lower the cost and time of workforce development and reduce execution risk as work continues to change. Thousands of organizations worldwide trust Skillsoft to power workforce readiness. Learn more at skillsoft.com.

About IDC MarketScape

The IDC MarketScape vendor assessment model is designed to provide an overview of the competitive fitness of technology and service suppliers in a given market. The research uses a rigorous scoring methodology based on qualitative and quantitative criteria, resulting in a single graphical illustration of each supplier’s position within a given market. IDC MarketScape provides a clear framework in which technology suppliers’ product and service offerings, capabilities and strategies, and current and future market success factors can be meaningfully compared. The framework also provides technology buyers with a 360-degree assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of current and prospective suppliers.
